title: In 1989 an earthquake did some of its worst damage 97 km away, on old landfill
body: The magnitude 6.9 Loma Prieta earthquake struck at 5:04 p.m. on 17 October 1989, from an epicentre in the Santa Cruz Mountains about 16 km north-east of Santa Cruz, California. The heaviest shaking there lasted about 15 seconds, yet some of the worst destruction came far to the north. San Francisco’s Marina District, about 97 km away, was built on landfill: its water-soaked mud, sand and rubble liquefied, and the shaking was stronger and lasted longer than on nearby rock. In Oakland, a double-decker freeway on former marshland, the Cypress Street Viaduct, collapsed and killed 42 people; in all, the earthquake was responsible for 63 deaths.

cover.alt: Computer-model map of the San Francisco Bay Area with a small coloured patch of shaking appearing near Santa Cruz

slides.alt: Computer simulation on a map of the San Francisco Bay Area: a patch of red and yellow appears in the hills near Santa Cruz and spreads outwards as a widening ring of green and blue, reaching San Jose, Palo Alto and finally San Francisco and Oakland, while a timer counts the seconds.
slides.caption: A USGS computer model of the 1989 Loma Prieta earthquake: colours show how hard the ground shakes as seismic waves spread from the Santa Cruz Mountains, reaching San Francisco in about 20 seconds.
slides.music: “Drums of the Deep” Kevin MacLeod (incompetech.com) · CC BY 4.0

slides.heading: How far from the epicentre
slides.note: Peak ground acceleration: over 0.6 g near the epicentre, up to 0.26 g in the Bay Area

left.label: On rock
left.text: The shaking was much less intense

right.label: On landfill or marsh
right.text: The shaking was amplified and lasted longer, and waterlogged soil liquefied

slides.prompt: Viewers across the US were watching a live TV broadcast when the earthquake hit. What was it?
slides.detail: Game 3, between the San Francisco Giants and the Oakland Athletics, was due to start at 5:35 p.m. at San Francisco’s Candlestick Park.

slides.question: Near the epicentre, how long did the heaviest shaking last?
slides.explanation: About 15 seconds in the Santa Cruz Mountains. On soft soils farther away, the shaking lasted longer.
